evals.prompt: We're a budget/value brand but want to do a big highway billboard takeover downtown to look impressive.
evals.expected_output: Should flag the brand-tier signal risk explicitly — premium DOOH placements (highway billboards, takeovers) send a positioning signal that a budget-tier brand's other marketing may not support. Should check marketing-strategy Section 14 and reference brand-tier-guide.md, and question whether this placement fits the brand's actual tier before proceeding.
assertions: Flags the brand-tier mismatch risk of premium DOOH for a budget-tier brand
Questions the placement choice rather than simply executing it

evals.prompt: Can you write billboard copy that explains our three key product benefits in detail?
evals.expected_output: Should push back on a detailed, multi-benefit message for a billboard format, explaining the extremely short dwell time constraint (2-3 seconds) and the one-idea, minimal-text (often 5-7 word) guideline. Should recommend picking a single idea and a large, legible headline instead of trying to convey three benefits.
assertions: Pushes back on a detailed multi-benefit billboard message
Explains the short dwell time / minimal text constraint specifically
Recommends narrowing to one clear idea
Does not simply write the requested multi-point copy as-is

evals.prompt: We ran a geofenced DOOH campaign and mobile data shows a lot of foot traffic near the billboard afterward. Should we scale this up?
evals.expected_output: Should caution against treating geofenced foot-traffic correlation as proof the placement caused the visits, noting this is a correlation not causation and referencing the incrementality-checkpoint. Should recommend a matched control area comparison before crediting DOOH with driving the traffic, especially before committing to a recurring/scaled placement based on it.
assertions: Distinguishes correlation (foot traffic near billboard) from proof of causation
Recommends this check specifically before scaling or recurring commitment
Does not endorse scaling based on the geofencing data alone

evals.prompt: We need to book a billboard for a launch happening in two weeks.
evals.expected_output: Should flag the lead-time risk explicitly — traditional/printed OOH generally requires longer lead time for booking and creative production (printed vinyl) than a two-week window typically allows. Should recommend either a programmatic DOOH (pDOOH) alternative for more flexibility and speed, or flag the timeline risk clearly if traditional format is required.
assertions: Flags the lead-time constraint of traditional/printed OOH for a two-week timeline
Recommends pDOOH as a faster alternative where speed matters
Does not assume a traditional billboard booking is achievable in two weeks without flagging risk
Distinguishes traditional vs. programmatic buying timelines
